hypothesis: Trailing 1-5 day residual returns (vs market + sector factors estimated on trailing data only) negatively predict next 1-5 day residual returns in liquid US large/mid caps, for moves not accompanied by material company news
signal_definition: z = -(sum of residual returns over last k_s days) / rolling residual vol; residual from rolling 120-day OLS on SPY + sector ETF (PCA-3 as second implementation); decision time 15:40 ET using 5-min bars through 15:40 plus daily data through t-1
universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members passing t-1 liquidity filter, no-news subsample
features: residual return, residual vol, abnormal turnover, news flags
model: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regression with Newey-West; decile long-short portfolio
parameters: k_s in {1,3,5}; OLS window 120; z-score window 60
expected_result: negative FM slope with |t|>=2; decile long-short gross return > 0
falsification_condition: FM slope not significantly negative (NW t < 2) OR decile long-short gross return <= 0 on the no-news subsample
actual_result: DEV 2005-01..2018-12 (daily, close-to-close forward returns, eligible PIT members): Fama-MacBeth slope of next-1d return on residual reversal score = +2.1e-4/unit z (NW t=5.54, 3,434 dates); k3/h3 t=3.99; k5/h5 t=3.04; top-minus-bottom decile spread 5.4 bp (h=1), 9.6 bp (h=3), 12.6 bp (h=10) per period. Sign convention: score = -residual, so a positive slope = reversal.
decision: NOT FALSIFIED (reversal present; news split pending Tier-1/2 flags)

hypothesis: Reversal is concentrated in low-abnormal-turnover movers; high-abnormal-turnover movers show continuation (Medhat & Schmeling 2022)
signal_definition: interaction of residual-return z-score with abnormal turnover tercile (turnover_t / trailing 60-day mean)
model: FM regression with interaction term; double sort
expected_result: negative coefficient in low-turnover tercile; non-negative/positive in high-turnover tercile
actual_result: DEV: FM slope by abnormal-turnover tercile: low 3.4e-4 (t=5.52), mid 2.6e-4 (t=5.29), high 1.6e-4 (t=3.68). Reversal strongest in low turnover but still positive in high turnover at the 1-day horizon; no continuation.
decision: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (monotone in turnover; no reversal-to-momentum flip at daily horizon)

hypothesis: Expected reversal return rises with lagged market volatility (Nagel 2012)
signal_definition: strategy return regressed on lagged VIX (or realized SPY vol) terciles
expected_result: positive slope; highest tercile earns most
actual_result: DEV no-news decile spread (h=1) by ex-ante lagged-VIX tercile (trailing 252-day rank): low 3.6 bp/day (t=2.62), mid 9.5 (t=3.63), high 9.1 (t=3.23); HAC regression on log VIX(t-1): +18.7 bp per log-unit, t=3.61.
decision: SUPPORTED: reversal premium rises with lagged volatility; VIX gating is a legitimate sizing candidate

hypothesis: Residual (factor-cleaned) reversal beats raw reversal risk-adjusted (Blitz et al. 2013; Da et al. 2014)
signal_definition: raw k-day return z-score vs residual k-day return z-score
model: decile portfolios; Sharpe comparison with bootstrap CI
actual_result: DEV FM t-stats: residual score 5.54 vs raw 1-day return score 3.97 (h=1); k3: 3.99 vs 3.81; k5: 3.04 vs 3.53. Decile-spread comparison pending (same-scale test).
decision: PROVISIONAL: residual >= raw at 1-3 day horizons; final call after decile comparison

hypothesis: Net-of-cost profitability survives in the most liquid tercile with turnover-aware construction (De Groot et al. 2012)
signal_definition: frozen DEV-selected construction applied to VAL
universe: most liquid tercile of PIT universe
falsification_condition: net Sharpe <= 0 under base costs on untouched VAL

hypothesis: Decay curve implies optimal holding <= 5 days; gross alpha per unit turnover falls monotonically beyond
signal_definition: IC and long-short return by forward horizon 1..20 days
expected_result: peak alpha per turnover at k <= 5
actual_result: DEV IC decay (k=1): 1.61% at h=1, 1.00% at h=5, 0.83% at h=10, 0.74% at h=15; decile spread 5.4/7.1/9.6/9.1/12.6 bp at h=1/2/3/5/10. Spread net of a ~4 bp round trip per day of holding peaks at h=3 (1.9 bp/day) vs h=1 (1.4), h=5 (1.0), h=10 (0.9).
decision: NOT FALSIFIED; holding horizon = 3 days selected from the decay curve (before any net-Sharpe search)

hypothesis: Residual reversal is materially stronger for no-news moves than for moves accompanied by material company news (8-K and/or article flag known by the decision time)
signal_definition: news flag = 8-K accepted since previous decision time OR FMP article/keyword hit before decision time; interaction with reversal signal
universe: as H1 (full universe, split by news flag)
features: news flags (Tier 1 8-K items; Tier 2 article counts 2012+)
model: FM regression with news interaction; filter ablation ladder
actual_result: DEV (daily model, Tier-1 8-K flags at the 16:00 decision time, avg 16.6 flagged eligible names/day): no-news FM slope +2.56e-4 (t=6.43, 3,434 dates), decile spread +6.8 bp/day; news-day FM slope -6.58e-4 (t=-2.17, 166 dates with >=30 flagged names), decile spread -15.4 bp/day. Tier-2 article flags pending (news pull in progress).
decision: SUPPORTED on Tier 1: reversal is a no-news phenomenon; news movers continue

hypothesis: Residual moves accompanied by material news show post-news drift (continuation) over 1-10 days (Chan 2003; Tetlock 2011)
signal_definition: news-mover subsample; forward residual return by horizon
falsification_condition: no significant positive drift on DEV
actual_result: DEV: earnings-8-K movers continue (FM slope -6.45e-4, t=-2.32, 243 dates); non-earnings 8-K movers show no drift (t=-0.22, 1,154 dates). Continuation sleeve candidate = post-earnings drift only.
decision: SUPPORTED for earnings news; NOT for other 8-K news

hypothesis: FALLBACK FAMILY (only if H1 is falsified): sector/industry-ETF residual returns vs SPY mean-revert at 1-5 days
signal_definition: ETF residual return z-score vs SPY
universe: liquid US sector/industry ETFs fixed by inception date and t-1 liquidity before download
model: pooled panel regression with Driscoll-Kraay SEs; top-3/bottom-3 rank long-short

hypothesis: Cost-model correction (not a strategy trial): market-impact term
parameters: pre-registered sqrt k=1 -> Almgren et al. (2005) k=0.142, beta=0.6; sqrt k=1 retained as stress variant
actual_result: At $1M capital and ~0.1% participation the sqrt/k=1 form charged ~6 bp per trade (1.5-2.2 bp/day), ~14x the Almgren et al. estimate (~0.45 bp). Corrected before any VAL/holdout run; observed DEV proxy results before correction: net SR -0.65 to -1.93.

hypothesis: Horizon refinement: where in event time does the no-news reversal accrue?
signal_definition: decile spread of score_k1 over windows close t+a -> t+b
actual_result: No-news decile spread: t->t+1 6.8 bp (t=5.63); t+1->t+2 1.7 bp (t=1.58); t+1->t+4 3.4 bp (t=1.81); t+2->t+5 1.7 bp (t=0.90). News movers: t->t+1 -15.4 bp (t=-3.79), later windows insignificant. The lagged daily proxy can only capture the weak tail; the MOC model at t is required. Holding candidates narrowed to {1,2,3} days for the MOC model.
decision: DIAGNOSTIC: day-1 capture is essential; horizon candidates {1,2,3}

hypothesis: Residualization method comparison for the reversal score (signal construction, DEV only)
expected_result: in-window residual best; lagged betas noisier
actual_result: Quintile spread bp/day (t): in-window OLS SPY+sector 5.2 (4.25); lagged SPY+sector 120d 4.3 (3.43); SPY-only beta 120d 4.3 (2.69); SPY-only beta 250d 5.1 (3.04); SPY-only 120d shrunk 50% to 1 4.8 (2.90); SPY+sector 250d 5.5 (4.19); SPY-only 60d 4.5 (2.78). Preview subset, 2005-2018.
decision: DIAGNOSTIC: choose the best ex-ante variant for the MOC score
